rationale: Both candidates independently rediscover the ground truth's core surviving concern (the engine hardcodes rel_l1_thresh=0.2, so the new 0.17 MiniMax-H3 default never takes effect) with strong, matching evidence, and both correctly confirm the partition-isolation fix (FL2VA-only hooking, Ref2VA rejection) is now sound. Y goes further with a rigorous, well-evidenced critique of the calibration polynomial's near-constant/non-monotone behavior and tighter secondary findings (memory footprint scaling, wasted RoPE computation, weak e2e cache-hit assertions, a drive-by unrelated test change), all clearly actionable. X's extra findings are more numerous but lower-value on average, including re-litigating the AMD CI failure that the ground truth reviewer already resolved as unrelated. Neither candidate flags the inline packed_total/attn_backend bugs, but those appear already fixed in the shown diff, so little recall is lost there for either.
